From 10b591e7fb7cdc8c1e53e9c000dc0ef7069aaa76 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date: Wed, 22 Oct 2025 11:06:36 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] f2fs: fix to avoid updating compression context during
 writeback

Bai, Shuangpeng <sjb7183@psu.edu> reported a bug as below:

Oops: divide error: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 11441 Comm: syz.0.46 Not tainted 6.17.0 #1 PREEMPT(full)
Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS 1.15.0-1 04/01/2014
RIP: 0010:f2fs_all_cluster_page_ready+0x106/0x550 fs/f2fs/compress.c:857
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 f2fs_write_cache_pages fs/f2fs/data.c:3078 [inline]
 __f2fs_write_data_pages fs/f2fs/data.c:3290 [inline]
 f2fs_write_data_pages+0x1c19/0x3600 fs/f2fs/data.c:3317
 do_writepages+0x38e/0x640 mm/page-writeback.c:2634
 filemap_fdatawrite_wbc mm/filemap.c:386 [inline]
 __filemap_fdatawrite_range mm/filemap.c:419 [inline]
 file_write_and_wait_range+0x2ba/0x3e0 mm/filemap.c:794
 f2fs_do_sync_file+0x6e6/0x1b00 fs/f2fs/file.c:294
 generic_write_sync include/linux/fs.h:3043 [inline]
 f2fs_file_write_iter+0x76e/0x2700 fs/f2fs/file.c:5259
 new_sync_write fs/read_write.c:593 [inline]
 vfs_write+0x7e9/0xe00 fs/read_write.c:686
 ksys_write+0x19d/0x2d0 fs/read_write.c:738
 do_syscall_x64 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63 [inline]
 do_syscall_64+0xf7/0x470 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f

The bug was triggered w/ below race condition:

fsync				setattr			ioctl
- f2fs_do_sync_file
 - file_write_and_wait_range
  - f2fs_write_cache_pages
  : inode is non-compressed
  : cc.cluster_size =
    F2FS_I(inode)->i_cluster_size = 0
   - tag_pages_for_writeback
				- f2fs_setattr
				 - truncate_setsize
				 - f2fs_truncate
							- f2fs_fileattr_set
							 - f2fs_setflags_common
							  - set_compress_context
							  : F2FS_I(inode)->i_cluster_size = 4
							  : set_inode_flag(inode, FI_COMPRESSED_FILE)
   - f2fs_compressed_file
   : return true
   - f2fs_all_cluster_page_ready
   : "pgidx % cc->cluster_size" trigger dividing 0 issue

Let's change as below to fix this issue:
- introduce a new atomic type variable .writeback in structure f2fs_inode_info
to track the number of threads which calling f2fs_write_cache_pages().
- use .i_sem lock to protect .writeback update.
- check .writeback before update compression context in f2fs_setflags_common()
to avoid race w/ ->writepages.

Fixes: 4c8ff7095bef ("f2fs: support data compression")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reported-by: Bai, Shuangpeng <sjb7183@psu.edu>
Tested-by: Bai, Shuangpeng <sjb7183@psu.edu>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/44D8F7B3-68AD-425F-9915-65D27591F93F@psu.edu
Signed-off-by: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jaegeuk Kim <jaegeuk@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/file.c b/fs/f2fs/file.c
index c045e38e60ee..6d42e2d28861 100644
--- a/fs/f2fs/file.c
+++ b/fs/f2fs/file.c
@@ -2128,8 +2128,9 @@ static int f2fs_setflags_common(struct inode *inode, u32 iflags, u32 mask)
 
 			f2fs_down_write(&fi->i_sem);
 			if (!f2fs_may_compress(inode) ||
-					(S_ISREG(inode->i_mode) &&
-					F2FS_HAS_BLOCKS(inode))) {
+				atomic_read(&fi->writeback) ||
+				(S_ISREG(inode->i_mode) &&
+				F2FS_HAS_BLOCKS(inode))) {
 				f2fs_up_write(&fi->i_sem);
 				return -EINVAL;
 			}

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/f2fs.h b/fs/f2fs/f2fs.h
index 575f9666c3b7..e69b01c1173a 100644
--- a/fs/f2fs/f2fs.h
+++ b/fs/f2fs/f2fs.h
@@ -947,6 +947,7 @@ struct f2fs_inode_info {
 	unsigned char i_compress_level;		/* compress level (lz4hc,zstd) */
 	unsigned char i_compress_flag;		/* compress flag */
 	unsigned int i_cluster_size;		/* cluster size */
+	atomic_t writeback;			/* count # of writeback thread */
 
 	unsigned int atomic_write_cnt;
 	loff_t original_i_size;		/* original i_size before atomic write */
@@ -4663,7 +4664,7 @@ static inline bool f2fs_disable_compressed_file(struct inode *inode)
 		f2fs_up_write(&fi->i_sem);
 		return true;
 	}
-	if (f2fs_is_mmap_file(inode) ||
+	if (f2fs_is_mmap_file(inode) || atomic_read(&fi->writeback) ||
 		(S_ISREG(inode->i_mode) && F2FS_HAS_BLOCKS(inode))) {
 		f2fs_up_write(&fi->i_sem);
 		return false;

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/data.c b/fs/f2fs/data.c
index eec691262fec..b92d362a02d6 100644
--- a/fs/f2fs/data.c
+++ b/fs/f2fs/data.c
@@ -3222,6 +3222,19 @@ static inline bool __should_serialize_io(struct inode *inode,
 	return false;
 }
 
+static inline void account_writeback(struct inode *inode, bool inc)
+{
+	if (!f2fs_sb_has_compression(F2FS_I_SB(inode)))
+		return;
+
+	f2fs_down_read(&F2FS_I(inode)->i_sem);
+	if (inc)
+		atomic_inc(&F2FS_I(inode)->writeback);
+	else
+		atomic_dec(&F2FS_I(inode)->writeback);
+	f2fs_up_read(&F2FS_I(inode)->i_sem);
+}
+
 static int __f2fs_write_data_pages(struct address_space *mapping,
 						struct writeback_control *wbc,
 						enum iostat_type io_type)
@@ -3267,10 +3280,14 @@ static int __f2fs_write_data_pages(struct address_space *mapping,
 		locked = true;
 	}
 
+	account_writeback(inode, true);
+
 	blk_start_plug(&plug);
 	ret = f2fs_write_cache_pages(mapping, wbc, io_type);
 	blk_finish_plug(&plug);
 
+	account_writeback(inode, false);
+
 	if (locked)
 		mutex_unlock(&sbi->writepages);
 

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/super.c b/fs/f2fs/super.c
index cb65ca90f9f6..d0b5791a1f8c 100644
--- a/fs/f2fs/super.c
+++ b/fs/f2fs/super.c
@@ -1759,6 +1759,7 @@ static struct inode *f2fs_alloc_inode(struct super_block *sb)
 	atomic_set(&fi->dirty_pages, 0);
 	atomic_set(&fi->i_compr_blocks, 0);
 	atomic_set(&fi->open_count, 0);
+	atomic_set(&fi->writeback, 0);
 	init_f2fs_rwsem(&fi->i_sem);
 	spin_lock_init(&fi->i_size_lock);
 	INIT_LIST_HEAD(&fi->dirty_list);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

**fs/f2fs/f2fs.h**
- Added a new field `atomic_t writeback` to `struct f2fs_inode_info` (line ~950). This counter tracks the number of threads currently executing `f2fs_write_cache_pages()` on the inode.
- Added a check for `atomic_read(&fi->writeback)` in the inline helper `f2fs_disable_compressed_file()` (line ~4667). If writeback is in progress, the function returns false, preventing the compression context from being disabled.

**fs/f2fs/super.c**
- In `f2fs_alloc_inode()`, the new `writeback` field is initialized to 0 via `atomic_set(&fi->writeback, 0)` (line ~1762).

**fs/f2fs/data.c**
- Added a static inline helper `account_writeback(struct inode *inode, bool inc)` (lines ~3225–3234). It acquires `i_sem` in read mode, then increments or decrements `fi->writeback` atomically depending on `inc`. The operation is guarded by `i_sem` to ensure proper ordering with other tasks updating the compression context.
- In `__f2fs_write_data_pages()`, calls `account_writeback(inode, true)` before `f2fs_write_cache_pages()` and `account_writeback(inode, false)` after it (lines ~3283 and ~3287). This marks that writeback is active during the page cache scanning.

**fs/f2fs/file.c**
- In `f2fs_setflags_common()`, when setting the compressed file flag, added a check `atomic_read(&fi->writeback)` to the existing conditions (line ~2131). If any writeback thread is active, the operation returns -EINVAL, preventing the compression context from being updated concurrently with writeback.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The core problem was a race: `f2fs_write_cache_pages()` could read `i_cluster_size` as 0 while another thread (via `set_compress_context` in `f2fs_setflags_common()`) was in the process of setting it to 4. This led to a division‑by‑zero when computing cluster indexes.

The solution introduces a **writeback in‑progress counter** (`fi->writeback`) that non‑atomically tracks whether any thread is inside `f2fs_write_cache_pages()`. This counter is updated under `i_sem` (acquired as read lock) to synchronize with the same lock used when modifying the compression context.

- **`data.c`** increments the counter before entering the critical writeback path and decrements it after leaving, ensuring that during the entire page‑cache scanning phase, the counter is non‑zero.
- **`file.c`** and **`f2fs.h`** (via `f2fs_disable_compressed_file()`) check this counter before allowing changes to the compression context. If writeback is active (`writeback > 0`), the context update is rejected with `-EINVAL` or `false`.
- Initialization in **`super.c`** ensures the counter starts at zero.

Together, these changes eliminate the race by preventing any modification of the compression context while writeback is in progress on the same inode. The `i_sem` lock provides the necessary ordering between the counter updates and the context changes.

The patch fixes a race condition where a divide-by-zero error occurs in `f2fs_all_cluster_page_ready` because the compression context (cluster size) gets updated by one thread while another thread is performing writeback, which relies on that context.

### Modifications per file:

- **`fs/f2fs/f2fs.h`**:
  - Added an `atomic_t writeback` field to `struct f2fs_inode_info` to track the number of threads currently executing writeback for that inode.
  - Updated `f2fs_disable_compressed_file()` to check `atomic_read(&fi->writeback)` (in addition to existing conditions) to prevent disabling compression while writeback is ongoing.

- **`fs/f2fs/super.c`**:
  - In `f2fs_alloc_inode()`, the new `writeback` atomic counter is initialized to `0` for each newly allocated inode.

- **`fs/f2fs/data.c`**:
  - Introduced a helper function `account_writeback()` that safely increments or decrements the `writeback` counter under the `i_sem` lock (read lock, allowing concurrent writeback). If the filesystem doesn't support compression, the function does nothing.
  - In `__f2fs_write_data_pages()`, calls `account_writeback(inode, true)` before starting writeback via `f2fs_write_cache_pages()`, and `account_writeback(inode, false)` after completion to balance the counter.

- **`fs/f2fs/file.c`**:
  - In `f2fs_setflags_common()`, when attempting to set compression flags, added a check for `atomic_read(&fi->writeback)` to reject the operation if any writeback thread is active, preventing race conditions that lead to the divide-by-zero.

### Relationships:
- All changes revolve around a new synchronization mechanism: a per-inode atomic counter `writeback` that indicates ongoing writeback activity.
- The counter is updated in the writeback path (`data.c`) and checked in the compression‑context modification paths (`file.c` for enabling compression, and `f2fs.h` for disabling compression).
- The `i_sem` mutex is used to protect updates to the counter (though only read‑locked for the counter itself). The compression context updates already require `i_sem` in write mode, so the atomic counter provides a cheap, non-blocking check to avoid modifying the context while writeback is in progress.
- Together, these changes prevent the race where a compression context change (setting `i_cluster_size` from 0 to 4) occurs between tagging pages for writeback and using the cluster size in `f2fs_all_cluster_page_ready`, thereby eliminating the division by zero.

The patch fixes a race condition in f2fs where updating the compression context (`i_cluster_size`) concurrently with writeback can cause a division by zero (`divide error`) in `f2fs_all_cluster_page_ready`. The fix introduces an atomic counter to track ongoing writeback threads and uses it to prevent compression context changes during writeback.

## Modifications per file

### `fs/f2fs/f2fs.h`
- Added a new field `atomic_t writeback` to `struct f2fs_inode_info` to count the number of threads currently executing `f2fs_write_cache_pages()`.
- In `f2fs_disable_compressed_file()`, added an additional condition `atomic_read(&fi->writeback)` to check if writeback is in progress before allowing compression to be disabled. This prevents disabling compression while a writeback thread is using the old cluster size.

### `fs/f2fs/file.c`
- In `f2fs_setflags_common()`, when setting the `F2FS_COMPR_FL` flag, added a check `atomic_read(&fi->writeback)` alongside existing checks (`f2fs_may_compress`, `F2FS_HAS_BLOCKS`). If writeback is active, the function returns `-EINVAL` to avoid modifying the compression context (including `i_cluster_size`) during writeback.

### `fs/f2fs/super.c`
- In `f2fs_alloc_inode()`, initialized the new `writeback` field with `atomic_set(&fi->writeback, 0)`.

### `fs/f2fs/data.c`
- Added a new inline function `account_writeback(struct inode *inode, bool inc)` that:
  - Returns immediately if the filesystem does not support compression.
  - Acquires the `i_sem` read lock to safely update the `writeback` atomic counter.
  - Increments or decrements the counter based on the `inc` parameter.
- In `__f2fs_write_data_pages()`, before calling `f2fs_write_cache_pages()`, `account_writeback(inode, true)` is invoked. After the writeback completes (after `blk_finish_plug`), `account_writeback(inode, false)` is invoked. This accurately tracks the start and end of writeback for each thread.

## Relationships between modifications
The core idea is to use a new atomic counter (`writeback`) to signal whether any writeback thread is actively scanning pages in `f2fs_write_cache_pages()`. The counter is updated under `i_sem` protection in `data.c` to avoid race conditions in increment/decrement. In `file.c` and `f2fs.h`, modifications to the compression context (setting the `F2FS_COMPR_FL` flag or disabling compression) now check this counter to refuse the operation if writeback is ongoing. This prevents the race where `set_compress_context()` sets `i_cluster_size` while `f2fs_write_cache_pages()` reads the stale zero value, causing the division by zero.

The initialization in `super.c` ensures every inode starts with a clean counter. The checks in `f2fs_disable_compressed_file()` and `f2fs_setflags_common()` provide mutual exclusion by rejecting compression context changes when writeback is active. The `account_writeback()` function provides a consistent, lock-based way to manage the counter around the writeback critical section.
